_metadata.purpose: Content verification of the no-DRI clinical-dose anchors in scripts/data/rda_optimal_uls.json (entries whose notes say 'No official DRI'). Each anchor claims to be the lower bound of the clinically effective daily dose.
_metadata.method: Every cited PMID fetched from PubMed (abstract) and Europe PMC (open-access full text); dose and outcome sentences read per compound; replacement evidence searched on PubMed where the cited sources did not support the anchor. Quotes are exact text re-checked live by verify_anchor_citations.py.

decision_rules.verified: A controlled human trial, meta-analysis or position stand shows benefit at the anchor dose, AND a targeted PubMed dose-ranging search (dose-response / low dose / different doses; RCT or meta-analysis) found no positive controlled trial at a lower daily dose. Eligible for graduated dose credit.
decision_rules.corrected: The evidence shows a lower (or different) lowest effective daily dose; anchor_proposed replaces the value. Eligible for graduated dose credit.
decision_rules.supported_uncontrolled: Only uncontrolled evidence at the anchor dose. Value kept; not eligible.
decision_rules.not_established: The cited and searched sources do not establish a lower bound (no dose-efficacy statement, null or mixed results, weight-based or much higher doses). Value kept; not eligible.

_metadata.lower_bound_check: Added after the first pass wrongly marked betaine 2.5 g verified: Olthof 2003 (PMID 14652361) lowered homocysteine at 1.5 g/day. Every graduation-eligible anchor was then re-searched for lower effective doses.

evidence.quote: randomly assigned to ingest 100 mg of chlorophyllin or a placebo three times a day for 4 months
Chlorophyllin consumption at each meal led to an overall 55% reduction (P = 0.036) in median urinary levels of this aflatoxin biomarker compared with those taking placebo

anchors.reason: RCT at 300 mg/day (100 mg three times daily) reduced a validated carcinogen biomarker versus placebo.

evidence.quote: ONS plus 800 mg beta-alanine (ONS800; n = 19)
Treatments were consumed twice per day for 12 weeks
These changes were significantly greater (p < 0.05) than the changes in ONS (-6.3%)
1.6 g BA/day significantly increased muscle carnosine within 2 weeks
The BA group received 3.2 g of beta-alanine per day
Daily supplementation with 4 to 6 g of beta-alanine for at least 2 to 4 weeks has been shown to improve exercise performance

anchors.reason: In older adults, 800 mg twice daily (1.6 g/day) added to a nutritional drink improved working capacity more than the drink alone, and 1.6 g/day raises muscle carnosine; 3.2 g/day and the ISSN 4-6 g/day are higher studied doses.

evidence.quote: After the subjects of 1.5 g HMB or placebo pills per day for 2 weeks
MVC torque was significantly higher in the HMB group than in the PL group
the typical 3 g daily dosage of HMB used in human studies

anchors.reason: 3 g/day is the typical studied dose (ISSN), but a placebo-controlled RCT at 1.5 g/day preserved strength and range of motion after eccentric exercise, so 1.5 g/day is the lowest effective dose found.

evidence.quote: a single daily large dose (1500 mg)
GS may have a small to moderate effect in reducing OA-related pain

anchors.reason: Meta-analysis of oral glucosamine sulfate trials at 1500 mg/day shows a small-to-moderate pain effect.

evidence.quote: Capsules containing 100 mg of GABA or dextrin as a placebo were used as test samples
the condition of 30 min after GABA intake diminished this decrease compared with the placebo condition

anchors.reason: Placebo-controlled trial at 100 mg showed an acute EEG/mood effect under mental stress; evidence is acute and small.

evidence.quote: randomized to receive either ubiquinol (200 or 100 mg/day) or placebo for 8 weeks
demonstrated a significantly increased FMD in both treated groups compared with the placebo group

anchors.reason: RCT: 100 mg/day improved endothelial function (FMD) versus placebo.

evidence.quote: Members of the NMN group consumed 250 mg/day NMN for 12 weeks
the NMN group had a significantly shorter 4-m walking time than the placebo group
The NMN group had improved sleep quality at 12 weeks relative to the placebo group
Walking distance increase during the six-minute walking test was statistically significantly higher in the 300 mg, 600 mg, and 900 mg groups compared to placebo

anchors.reason: The originally cited 250 mg/day RCT (35479740) measured safety and blood NAD+ only, so it does not support a clinical anchor. A below-anchor search found a placebo-controlled RCT at 250 mg/day with between-group clinical outcomes (shorter 4-m walking time, better PSQI sleep scores); its primary stepping-test endpoint was null. The dose-ranging RCT was positive from 300 mg/day. 250 mg/day is the lowest dose with a positive controlled clinical outcome, so the anchor stays at 250 mg/day. The evidence is mixed: other 250 mg/day trials were null or only nominally significant. The 2026-09-15 follow-up audit's correction to 300 mg/day was reverted because it did not search below 300 mg/day.

evidence.quote: Subjects were orally given 20 mg of BioPQQ™ per day or placebo, for 12 weeks
the change of Stroop interference ratios (SIs) for the PQQ group was significantly smaller than for the placebo group
PQQ disodium salt: 21.5 mg/day
Significant improvements were observed on the Cognitrax
There were no significant differences between groups in aerobic performance after endurance-training

anchors.reason: A placebo-controlled RCT of 20 mg/day PQQ disodium salt (BioPQQ) found a significant between-group benefit on the Stroop test, and a second placebo-controlled RCT was positive for cognition at 21.5 mg/day. The 20 mg/day exercise RCT was null for performance, so the benefit is cognitive. No positive controlled trial below 20 mg/day was found, so 20 mg/day is the lowest effective dose. The 2026-09-15 follow-up audit's correction to 21.5 mg/day was reverted because it missed the 20 mg/day cognition RCT.

evidence.quote: low-dose berberine (< 1 g/d) achieve promising effects of FPG
Berberine 0.3 g tid

anchors.reason: Meta-analysis of T2DM RCTs includes 900 mg/day arms (0.3 g three times daily) and reports glucose effects below 1 g/day.

evidence.quote: there was a significant systolic BP and diastolic BP-reducing effect in randomized controlled trials with doses ≥500 mg/day

anchors.reason: Meta-analysis: blood-pressure effect only at >=500 mg/day, none below.

evidence.quote: improved attention compared with placebo in middle-aged women [250 mg/d for 1 mo
Individuals receiving citicoline exhibited improved attention

anchors.reason: Placebo-controlled trials at 250 mg/day improved attention (middle-aged women; adolescent males at 250 or 500 mg/day).

evidence.quote: Fasting plasma homocysteine after 6-wk daily intakes of 1.5, 3 and 6 g of betaine was 12% (P < 0.01), 15% (P < 0.002) and 20% (P < 0.0001) less than in the placebo group, respectively
randomly assigned to either a betaine (2.5 g/day; n = 11) or placebo
Supplementation with at least 4 g/d of betaine for a minimum of six weeks may moderately increase plasma TC

anchors.reason: A placebo-controlled 6-week trial lowered fasting homocysteine at 1.5 g/day (dose-dependently to 6 g/day), so 1.5 g is the lowest effective daily dose found; 2.5 g/day is the common sports-trial dose. The previously cited sources used 4-6 g/day, one reporting a cholesterol increase.

evidence.quote: 3 g of glycine or placebo were ingested
In subjects given glycine, the VAS data showed a significant reduction in fatigue

anchors.reason: Placebo-controlled trial at 3 g before bed reduced daytime fatigue after sleep restriction.

evidence.quote: pantethine supplementation for 16 weeks (600 mg/d for weeks 1-8 then 900 mg/d for weeks 9-16) is safe and significantly lowers TC and LDL-C
is achieved at a 300 mg twice per day dose schedule

anchors.reason: Two RCTs starting at 600 mg/day lowered LDL-C; authors report optimal benefit at 300 mg twice daily.

evidence.quote: Average peak torque in the hamstring skeletal muscle was significantly increased in both UA 500 mg (+12%, p = 0.027 compared with placebo)
non-significant improvements (4.30% and 3.90%, respectively) in PPO (the primary endpoint)

anchors.reason: RCT: 500 mg/day improved hamstring strength versus placebo (secondary endpoint; primary endpoint not met).

evidence.quote: allocated to a 3.2 g/day of whey protein (WP, N = 8) or BC (N = 10)
Post-exercise EIMD may be reduced and performance better maintained by a low dose of BC administration
supplemented with a relatively low dose (0.5-1.0 g/day) of bovine colostrum (COL) or placebo (PBO)
10 g/day bovine colostrum protein concentrate (CPC)

anchors.reason: A double-blind RCT at 3.2 g/day (whey control) maintained performance and lowered inflammatory markers; 10-20 g/day trials are higher doses. A 0.5-1.0 g/day trial reported fewer self-reported respiratory symptom days only in a higher-risk subgroup, too weak to anchor on.

evidence.quote: taking 1 g/day of MgT or placebo for 21 days
MgT significantly (p < 0.05) improved vs placebo deep sleep score
subjects between 50 and 70 kg took 1.5 g/day

anchors.reason: A 2024 RCT showed benefit at 1 g/day; the 1.5 g/day figure came from weight-based dosing (1.5-2 g/day) in the earlier cognition trial.

evidence.quote: Both groups of participants took 10 tablets, each containing 200 mg MSM or lactose, per day for 12 weeks
MSM oral consumption improved both knee and systemic health conditions
MSM (3g twice a day) improved symptoms of pain and physical function
Three grams of MSM administered daily did not provide significant improvements

anchors.reason: No positive trial of MSM alone at 1.5 g/day was found; the lowest positive placebo-controlled dose is 2 g/day (knee quality of life). Results at 3 g/day are mixed; 6 g/day improved OA pain.

evidence.quote: daily HA (120 mg) intake for 12 weeks
skin condition was significantly improved in terms of wrinkle assessment
received oral HA (120 mg/day)
SH120 significantly enhanced skin hydration and elasticity
The subjects in the HA group were given 200 mg of HA once a day everyday for 12 months
WOMAC pain (primary efficacy variable) was similar in both study groups

anchors.reason: Previous references were an injection-versus-NSAID review (32047830) and a multi-ingredient krill product (37686801). Placebo-controlled oral trials are positive at 120 mg/day (skin) and 200 mg/day (knee OA); the 80 mg/day trial did not beat placebo on its primary outcome.

evidence.quote: supplementation with DIM 100 mg × 1/day in BRCA carriers was associated with a significant decline in FGT amount on MRI

anchors.reason: Only a single-arm study (breast-density biomarker) at 100 mg/day; no controlled trial.

evidence.quote: Further investigations will show if there is a significant effect in patients suffering from atopic eczema
on the base of 250 to 600 mg/day γ-linolenic acid

anchors.reason: Cited sources are a pharmacokinetic study and a narrative review suggesting 250-600 mg/day for mastalgia; nothing supports 120 mg/day as an effective dose.

evidence.quote: evening primrose oil was supplied as 500-mg oval clear unmarked capsules
received a daily dose of 1.5 g evening primrose oil or placebo for three months

anchors.reason: 500 mg is the capsule size, not a daily dose; trials in the review use 1.5-3 g/day. A lower bound is not established from the cited sources.

evidence.quote: the effects of a single dose of citrulline malate (CM)

anchors.reason: Neither cited abstract states a dose and neither full text is open access.

evidence.quote: evidence supporting acute improvements in vasodilation and skeletal muscle tissue perfusion after supplementation is scarce and inconsistent

anchors.reason: The only cited source is a review without a dose-efficacy statement in its abstract; full text not open access.

evidence.quote: melatonin gradually reduces sleep onset latency and increases total sleep time, peaking at 4 mg/day

anchors.reason: Dose-response meta-analyses do not state a lower effective bound; melatonin dose is scored by the sleep-support adapter, not the generic window.

evidence.quote: found that NAC was no more effective than placebo

anchors.reason: Cited sources are psychiatric reviews without a dose-efficacy statement; the bipolar meta-analysis found no benefit over placebo.

evidence.quote: The daily dose of SAMe varied from 200 to 3200 mg
showed no significant difference in depression with SAMe compared to the comparison treatment

anchors.reason: Doses ranged 200-3200 mg with no significant effect; the Cochrane review found no high-quality evidence.

evidence.quote: insufficiently evaluated to assess their effectiveness

anchors.reason: Meta-analyses report heterogeneous dosing and insufficient evaluation; no lower bound.

evidence.quote: a small dose of EAAs stimulates muscle mTORC1 signaling and MPS

anchors.reason: Cited sources are acute muscle-protein-synthesis experiments (6.8 g and 5 g), not clinical outcome trials.

evidence.quote: Subgroup analysis showed a significant reduction in intestinal permeability with doses over 30g/day

anchors.reason: The cited meta-analysis found effects only above 30 g/day; trials dose by body weight (0.25-0.5 g/kg). 5 g/day is not supported.
